target_customer: Presenters, teachers, universities and enterprises that want live audience polling inside slide decks
problem: Audience response clickers were expensive hardware; polling could be done cheaply with the phones people already carry.
business_model: SaaS subscription by audience size and plan
product_category: Audience response and live polling software

founders.name: Jeff Vyduna
founders.background_notes: A profile says he and Gessler met as consultants at Deloitte; YC page says the company was unfunded after YC. Stepped back to the board in 2022.

founders.name: Brad Gessler
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as co-founder and CTO; later co-founded Gbrain.io.

founders.name: Sean Eby
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder; later investor and engineering leader at ServiceCore.

competitors.name: Clicker audience response systems (Turning Technologies TurningPoint)
competitors.what: Hardware clickers plus PowerPoint plugin for classroom and meeting polling

technical_complexity.rationale: Web app plus SMS short code aggregation; carrier integration was the main hurdle.

defensibility.rationale: Easy to copy; Turning Technologies shipped a phone app in 2009, and slide-deck plugins created modest switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Turning Technologies launched ResponseWare for phones around 2009; Poll Everywhere kept growing independently.

market_need_then: Clickers cost far more than using audience cell phones; the CEO said in 2009 they were the first to realize this could be done cheaply with phones.

branding.domain_note: polleverywhere.com; pollev.com short domain used for participants.

identity.logo: Logo not described by an opened source

branding.brand_signature: Poll Everywhere works everywhere and the PollEv.com short link
branding.community_and_virality: Used widely by universities (many host guides); a sister brand Survey Everywhere was launched on its platform.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name tied to a clear job and wide education adoption, but no mascot or fan culture found.

outcome_analysis: Poll Everywhere replaced clickers with phone-based polling, took only about 20K from YC, and grew by bootstrapping into a company of about 70 serving 82 percent of the Fortune 500 by its own claim. Founders moved to the board in 2022 under new executives. Debt-only financing and no equity rounds point to capital efficiency rather than a venture exit.
notes: The 20K YC round and Lowercase Capital rest on CB Insights and Wikipedia mirrors. The 2020 1M debt rests on ZoomInfo alone (PPP-linked, unverified); Caplight lists 1.65M total dated February 2021. Founding date conflicts (April 2007 code start vs 2008). Acquired TextTheMob and ClassMetric in 2012 (EdSurge).
